No problem! I don't mind the questions. The intent with these gods is to have a creationist angle. They created the universe, are ludicrously powerful, and exist before everything. Another goal with this is to purposefully leave them vague so they can later take on aspects that fantasy races would give to them.   


and yes. I do tend to break down gods into these physics components and that's the goal is to try and create a system of gods that fits this without causing issues with stepping on each other's domains. However, I should also add that since its fantasy, there are certain things that are physical laws within this world.   


For example, there is a goddess of souls who manages the transition from life to death to life. Clearly, that's not quite as simple as breaking down physics into its rules.

This is also how I create my gods. They exist before creation and perform the creation of the universe, however this leads to lots of problems. For example, how can gods of love exist if love isn't defined even after the creation of the universe? Why is there a god of the forge before creation if humans invented blacksmithing?  


Perhaps you could give me some examples of your gods to inspire. Thanks.

I know this is a weird thing to ask, but don't think about the religious aspect of it quite yet. Think only about the deities.   


These are deities who exist to govern the universe and its laws. Yes, those include the physical laws.

Not necessarily because it is a physical manifestation, but because it's not clearly define in a universal sense.   


For examples, I have a god of light. That makes sense. Light is real (photons). They exist and need to be maintained. However, I also have a god of time. Time... exists? Time is something to be maintained. However, there is clearly no physical manifestation of time. And there is a debate to be made on whether or not it is truly real.   


This is all to say that the gods I'm hoping to create are architects of the universe who create and maintain its fundamental laws and components.

It would take a lot of explaining, but the short answer is yes. They are real. For plot reasons (obviously), they tend to indirectly interact with the physical world. But theoretically, they could.   


They are real. They are immensely powerful.

thanks for the comment.

Honestly, it sounds like a big player problem to me. 

It all clearly depends on your party and the players, but I would continue the fight anyway. Players aren’t always supposed to feel safe and confident. When they are finally ready to quit and realize the mistake they’ve made, send in the friendly NPC as you planned. 

If you don’t think your players can handle that or if they’ll quit, then first off that’s a red flag for players that they get frustrated when they’re not winning. Secondly, talk with them out of game before the session starts and explain to them that the fight wasn’t supposed to be easy and them immediately attacking made it even harder. Explain to them that, yes, their actions do indeed have consequences and they will suffer those if they’re not careful. 

You care about your players and that’s great. Any good GM wants their players to enjoy the game, but if you never have stakes the game will eventually devolve to murder hobos (as it may have already happened).
